detail.longDescription: Most type checkers support reveal_type(expr) *, to show the inferred type of expr : typing. reveal_type ( obj , / ) Ask a static type checker to reveal the inferred type of an expression. [...] Most type checkers support reveal_type() anywhere, even if the name is not imported from typing . I don't understand its purpose. Can't I just write expr ? In either case, I hover over expr in my IDE to see its inferred type: value = 10 value # (variable) value: Literal[10] reveal_type(value) # Type of "value" is "Literal[10]" Is there a difference? Why is there a need for reveal_type() ? * Note: I'm not asking about typing.reveal_type() which is imported from typing and has runtime behaviour. I'm asking about the type-checking-only "pseudo-global" reveal_type() (which would raise a NameError at runtime).
